## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-scheduled, branchless-blend per-particle update with hash RNG can approach the streaming ceiling on identity-ordered workloads.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈963) falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so the L1d regime is unseen. The L2 spill (N≈61680) sits at the N=65000 sample. At q=0.01 the curve is essentially FLAT across the spill: 57.5 ns/p at N=65000, 55.3 at N=262000, 62.7 at N=1M, 48.2 at N=4M — no knee, just noise. Death rate raises the floor slightly (q=0.25 averages ~40 ns/p vs ~55 at q=0.01 at large N) without changing the N-shape. The 26.9 ns/p outlier at N=4000/q=0.25 likely reflects early loop exit when most particles die. No cache-spill knee is visible; cost is dominated by per-particle compute, not memory latency.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.53 GB/s (N=4000, q=0.25) = 10% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, but that point is the anomalous early-exit outlier. Excluding it, the best is 1.87 GB/s (N=4M, q=0.25) = 7.4% of ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound at every measured N and death rate and never transitions toward bandwidth-bound. Achieved bandwidth rises slightly with N (1.1→1.41 GB/s at q=0.01) as fixed overhead amortizes, but even at N=4M it remains an order of magnitude below ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle loop: only 2 of 354 instructions carry vector suffixes (`movi.2d` for zero-init). FP math is scalar — `ldp s4, s5`, `fadd s4`, `fmul s4`, `fcvtzs` all in 32-bit s-registers. The render path is a scalar scatter: `ldrb`/`strb` byte loads and stores into the framebuffer at computed offsets (`lsl x0, x0, #2; add x0, x23, x0`) with `csel`-based clamping to 0xFF. There is no gather. The `bl _halide_b1` call delegates walk1 to a Halide function, but the inlined render scatter's byte-granular stores and scalar clamping dominate, capping bandwidth far below ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 10% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling (2.53 GB/s at the anomalous N=4000/q=0.25 point; 1.87 GB/s = 7.4% at N=4M/q=0.25). The scalar, unvectorized codegen with byte-granular framebuffer scatter (`strb`, `ldrb`, `csel`) prevents streaming regardless of death rate or N, and no cache-spill knee appears. The Halide branchless blend does not approach the streaming ceiling.
